doc.title: Lonnie Liston Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 9, 2021

title: Rhythm sections out of sync and Miles's advice
summary: When bass and drums disagree, the pianist must adjust; Miles told a young bassist that if they play fast, you play slow.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. Have you ever been in a rhythm section where the bass player and the drummer didn’t seem to be on the same page?

Oh yeah well that happened a lot. You know so then you’ve really got to be flexible. You know you’ve got to listen to both and you might have to just get in the middle. Because I remember, what’s the guy’s name who was working with Miles, the bass player. Not Ron Carter, before Ron, oh he’s really an excellent bass player.

No not Paul, it was after Paul, and I guess it will come back to me. But he’s really great. So he was in the group and I think Herbie was doing one thing and I think Tony Williams was playing it — you know Tony what is 18, 19, 20? He’s doing something else. So he asked Miles, “What am I supposed to do?” Miles said, “You just, you have to be, if they play fast you play slow.” I mean you have to really adjust.
